text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-President Hrawi defines the mandate of the coming government after the resignation of the current cabinet in the wake of recent parliamentary elections.
-Port of Beirut signed a $102-million contract with Spanish company to renovate its facilities; the first stage will end within a year.
-Hrawi's consultations with the new MPs to nominate new prime minister will take place on October 23, and the nomination of the new prime minister will be on the 24th or 26th of this month.

-The five-nation committee monitoring a ceasefire agreement in Lebanon visited Safad al-Batikh, a south Lebanon village where 10 people were wounded by weekend Israeli shelling. Evidence of Israel using internationally-banned shells in the bombardment.
-Israeli soldier wounded in a mysterious accident in south Lebanon.
-Hrawi says peace and stability in Lebanon will not be strengthened with the spreading of corruption in the public administration.
-Parliament Speaker Berri will head to Damascus to meet Syrian president Hafez Assad and prime minister Hariri headed to Paris en route to Washington to meet President Bill Clinton on Friday.
-Hariri says the new government must make social policy a top priority.
